attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own newsletter post, not a quote of anyone else.

semantics.note: Revision 2 keeps 'it seems', 'acceleration' and the wording about the market's appetite. It is a forecast-like impression hedged by 'it seems', with no deadline.

contract.note: The contract rightly treats the hedged, undated impression as not adjudicable. The same passage also concedes that more raises could extend the cycle.

evidence.note: Oct 2024 report of a $6.6B OpenAI raise. Cuts against 'funding will not be there', but cannot score a hedged, undated claim.
Mar 2025 report of a $40B round. Strong investor appetite, but context only for a hedged impression.

reviews.rationale: The whole sentence is hedged by 'it seems', gives no deadline, and leaves 'collapse' undefined. The passage also openly allows further fundraising. Under the policy, hedged language is not scored. Later funding (e1, e2) is noted as context only.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: The wording is close to the source. But this is a sweeping judgement in a passage calling for the industry to 'atone', not a testable observation. Better classed as rhetoric.

contract.note: 'Always unsustainable', 'stealing', 'vague' and 'overstated' have no measure. Scoring them would mean inventing definitions, so not adjudicable is fair.

reviews.rationale: Four value-laden characterizations with no metric, period or threshold. 'Stealing' is a contested legal and moral label. No evidence was gathered, and none could settle the claim without supplied definitions.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: A statement about the state of things when he wrote it. The nearness implied by 'not quite' is rightly left untested.

contract.note: Uses the speaker's own definition of the popping (OpenAI's collapse, Microsoft and VC cutting it off). A fair, ordinary plain reading.

evidence.note: Late Aug 2024 report (citing WSJ) that Thrive and Microsoft were lining up to fund OpenAI. No cut-off.
Aug 29, 2024 report (citing Bloomberg) that OpenAI was close to a round valuing it above $100B.
On the post date OpenAI was operating normally, though senior staff were leaving.

reviews.rationale: In August 2024 OpenAI was operating and in active funding talks, with venture capital and Microsoft expected to take part. That is the opposite of the collapse the speaker defined as the popping, so 'not yet popped' holds for the period.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: 'Will have to come through' is firm language about where funding would come from, with a horizon of end-2025. The $5–10B need is kept but cannot be observed.

contract.note: Testing the named sources against Microsoft and VC is a fair plain reading. Treating bank revolving credit as context is reasonable. Whether 'have to' means only or main sources affects the result.

evidence.note: The Oct 2024 $6.6B round was led by Thrive, a venture capital firm, not by Saudi Arabia, SoftBank or private debt.
Microsoft, Nvidia and VC firms took part. SoftBank gave only $500M, and no Saudi investor is named.
OpenAI's own disclosure of a $4B undrawn bank revolver. Bank debt, not clearly private debt.
SoftBank led the Mar 2025 round with $30B of $40B. Microsoft and VC firms still took part.

reviews.rationale: The deadline has passed. The SoftBank part holds: SoftBank led and largely funded the 2025 round. The rest fails: the first raise after the post, which covered the stated $5–10B need, was VC-led with Microsoft taking part. No Saudi participation is shown, and no private-debt financing is shown. Microsoft and VC did not stand back.
